design.existing_patterns: Retain the existing TypeScript server, SQLite receipts and observations, bounded provider adapters, React/Vite research desk, offline startup verifier, and project-record ETL gate.
design.data_ownership: Provider data remains subject to provider-specific access and retention; local SQLite is controlled by the local operator. Unknown-provenance historical rows remain quarantined and are never relabeled. The first-run archive contains a public SEC filing reference plus one actual Jev output from the operator-authorized isolated smoke; exact account terms and spending controls remain unverified.
design.boundaries: Network collection and Jev forwarding default off; source and account approvals are distinct; the read-only first-run endpoint serves a separately typed archival record only when all-time eligible observation history is zero, and never inserts it into Desk data or calculations. Live smoke uses a temporary isolated database; Radar stays disabled.
design.simplicity: Use the existing React controls, formatters, tests, and verifiers; no new runtime dependency or synthetic product fixture is introduced.

Link the filing, label receipt and digest values as recorded references that cannot be resolved from this installation, keep the archive outside Desk observations, counts, charts, usage, and alerts, and say it is independently unreviewed and unvalidated. first_run.empty_or_blocked_state: Loading and API failure stay unknown, not empty. Any all-time eligible saved observation suppresses the archive even if stale; a newly arrived local observation suppresses it immediately. Demo/test and legacy_unknown rows never qualify as research observations. If the archive is unavailable, show the actual empty or blocked state and current source/JeV gate without implying live collection or scoring.
